item.text:
The locality and cylinder arguments are coherent once several missing invariants are promoted to assumptions. The package does avoid the advertised run-inspection circularity, and the Eisenstein countermodel is correctly guarded out. But it is not a self-contained proof for an internally defined total machine: the definition of lawful sites is incomplete, harvest totality is asserted, and SPAN’s decisive saturation identity is not derivable from the supplied definitions.

### 1. Machine definition and totality

> “Φ₀ = a monic lift, prescribed by a fixed policy from level-0 data only, of an irreducible factor φ̄ of the reduction f̄”

**JUSTIFICATION GAP.** Under the package’s own box convention, level 0 means reduction modulo \(p^0\), which contains no information about \(\bar f\). Presumably “level-0 data” means residue-field/mod-\(p\) data, but as written the root policy has incompatible inputs.

> “LAWFUL(H) is the conjunction of the machine's structural laws … transition admissibility … canonical presentation…”

> “The only property of LAWFUL used … is that it does not mention f”

**JUSTIFICATION GAP.** LAWFUL is not actually defined: “transition admissibility,” “span-entry,” “vertex-transport,” and “canonical root” are names rather than predicates. Consequently one cannot audit whether the stated record laws are consistent, whether lawful successors exist, or whether lawfulness enforces needed arithmetic conditions such as
\[
\gamma-s_0h\equiv0\pmod e.
\]

This matters immediately for:

> “\(L(H):=1+\max\lceil I_i/E_i\rceil\in\mathbb N\).”

The displayed node laws allow arbitrary \(\gamma\in\mathbb Z\). Hence all \(I_i\) may be negative enough that \(L(H)\le0\). Nothing displayed proves \(L(H)\in\mathbb N\). Theorem 1’s modulus \(p^L\) is therefore not defined for every site known from the supplied definition to be lawful. One may assume the omitted lawfulness rules exclude this, but it is not proved here.

> “The successor key … determined by \(\nu_i\)'s recorded data and the policy”

> “nothing here proves the policy exists, is canonical, or is unique”

**JUSTIFICATION GAP.** This is honest conditionality, but it defeats the description “explicitly defined OM read machine” and prevents an audit of totality. The results are per any policy satisfying M4, not yet for a supplied total policy.

> “(M6) Harvest totality … every … pair yields a node that is LAWFUL and READ-realized on \(f\).”

> “[Definition … for the harvested clauses (R1)–(R3)]”

**JUSTIFICATION GAP.** READ also contains R5. Harvesting R1–R3 does not definitionally establish the transported-vertex requirement R5, nor the unnamed lawfulness conditions. Thus M6 is a substantive existence/correctness invariant, not merely a definition. Theorems 2(b) and 3 are conditional on it.

There is also an ambiguity in R5:

> “the \(\Phi_{i+1}\)-development … has … a coefficient whose height-\(\beta_i^*\) residual…”

The valuation used for that coefficient is not stated. Theorem 1 treats it as a \(w_i\)-graded residual with stretch \(E_i\). That interpretation must be made explicit.

### 2. D-14 and the lawful-site quantifier

The central noncircularity claim is valid conditional on M4 and M5.

> “The proof never inspects the run of \(f\) or \(f′\) — the site supplies its own keys and heights through its records.”

Correct. The proof assumes READ on one polynomial only to transfer the fixed list of constraints attached to an already supplied site. It does not discover the site by executing either canonical run, and it does not assume the site belongs to the reference tree. That is exactly the quantifier needed for a later no-missing argument.

The transfer of R1 and R2 is sound: from
\[
w_i(B_j-B'_j)\ge LE_i>I_i
\]
all valuations and graded residues at heights at most \(I_i\) are preserved. The separate zero-coefficient cases are handled correctly.

For R5:

> “the \(\Phi_{i+1}\)-development transfers by DEV … the … residual transfers by (†) + R-LOC”

**JUSTIFICATION GAP.** Inequality (†) was written for the coefficients of the \(\Phi_i\)-development. DEV and POS do give the analogous bound for the \(\Phi_{i+1}\)-development, but that bound must be rederived; it is not literally (†). This is a small omitted step, assuming the intended valuation in R5 is \(w_i\).

Thus D-14 genuinely avoids run inspection, but its “all lawful sites” formulation remains conditional on the missing definition of LAWFUL and the unproved nonnegativity of its ceiling.

### 3. SPAN’s weight ledger

#### W-ADD

> “the residual polynomial has degree \(wSide/e\)”

This follows from the recorded endpoint conditions \(pat(0)\ne0\) and \(pat(wSide/e)\ne0\).

> “\(\sum_\psi g_\psi\mu_\psi=wSide/e\)”

Correct factor-degree accounting.

> “A child … has \(wt(child)=\deg\Phi_o\,e\,g_\psi\,\mu_\psi\)”

Correct under the stated successor-key degree formula and the rule that the child window width is \(\mu_\psi\).

> “\(\sum\) over children on ONE face … \(=\deg\Phi_o\,wSide\)”

Correct only if the roster contains every irreducible factor with its full multiplicity. That is precisely the substantive harvest-totality part of M6.

> “\(\sum\) over ALL recorded children … \(=\deg\Phi_o\cdot(\text{total recorded span})\le wt(o)\)”

Correct provided the recorded faces really are distinct faces of one lower polygon. Their interiors are then disjoint. Equality of total interval length with \(W_o\) does imply exact coverage of \([0,W_o]\), not merely inclusion.

#### L-SAT

> “the saturation identity \(accE\cdot accF=Dwidth\cdot\mu\) says exactly: verdict degree \(=\deg\Phi_H\cdot\mu_H\)”

**JUSTIFICATION GAP.** Neither `accE`, `accF`, nor `Dwidth` is defined in a way connecting it to \(\deg\Phi_H\). The equality needed by the proof is
\[
\text{leaf verdict degree}=wt(\text{leaf}),
\]
but the displayed saturation clause supplies that only if `Dwidth = deg Φ_H` and the verdict degree is definitionally `accE·accF`. Those identifications are asserted here, not derived from §1.

#### Induction and contradiction

Given W-ADD and L-SAT, the induction is correct:

1. A leaf contributes exactly its weight.
2. Each interior subtree contributes at most the sum of child weights.
3. W-ADD bounds that sum by the parent weight.
4. A proper span produces a strictly positive deficit.
5. Equality at a root forces no deficit anywhere below it.

The final equality step nevertheless relies on another underspecified clause:

> “(F6) says T's per-track leaf degrees match exactly these multiplicities — i.e. the track subtree's verdict total equals its root weight”

**JUSTIFICATION GAP.** F6 says only that leaf degrees “match the repeated-factor multiplicities.” It does not formally state the sum identity \(m\deg\bar\phi\). The alternative F3+F5 argument works if “simple part,” track partition, and verdict degrees have the asserted degree interpretation, but those relations are likewise not fully defined.

SPAN is therefore a valid ledger conditional on two missing degree identities. It is not “proved outright from the definitions” as claimed in §8.

### 4. CYL, scaling, and disjointness

Conditional on Theorem 2(b), the cylinder argument is exact.

> “membership is constant on level-\(t\) cylinders”

This yields both directions because the forward implication is universally quantified: after proving it with either box as the fibered starting box, the variables may be exchanged.

> “\(\Phi_N(T)\) is the full preimage of \(\Phi_t(T)\)”

Correct. This is stronger than mere inclusion and supports the claimed exact union.

> “The reduction map … is exactly \(p^{n(N-t)}\)-to-1”

Correct: a monic degree-\(n\) polynomial has exactly \(n\) free coefficients, each with \(p^{N-t}\) lifts. Hence the factor is \(p^{n(N-t)}\), not \(p^{(n+1)(N-t)}\).

> “(F1) forces chains(T) = chains(T″)”

This establishes per-box uniqueness of the entire recorded histories, assuming “chains” include their node records. F2, F3, and ns-freeness then determine the remaining tree payload. Thus distinct nonempty fibers are disjoint.

The finiteness sentence is slightly imprecise because trees have varying thresholds \(t\), but disjointness at the common level \(N\) repairs it: every nonempty tree with threshold at most \(N\) owns at least one distinct level-\(N\) box. Empty-fiber trees may indeed be omitted from the count.

### 5. Eisenstein countermodel

The guards exclude \(X^n+p^N\) versus \(X^n\) exactly where claimed.

The root face has intercept \(I=N\), so its ceiling is
\[
L=1+\lceil N\rceil=N+1.
\]
The two polynomials are congruent modulo \(p^N\), but not modulo \(p^{N+1}\). Therefore Theorem 1 is inapplicable to that comparison.

For Theorems 2(b) and 3:

- The zero polynomial decode \(X^n\) has no slot-0 pin and reaches an ns-halt, so it is outside the decided ns-free fiber hypothesis.
- The Eisenstein tree records the deep face, giving threshold at least \(N+1\); its locality/cylinder conclusions apply only at working precision at least that threshold.
- Comparing it to the zero box at level \(N\) is therefore below the theorem’s threshold.

This is precisely the guarded/unguarded distinction. The package does not accidentally reassert the refuted cross-level locality.

VERDICT: SOUND-WITH-GAPS
